# truenas_snapshot_clone (Resource)

Creates a writable ZFS clone of a snapshot (pool.snapshot.clone). The clone is a new dataset or zvol that shares blocks with the snapshot until either is written to, so it is created instantly and costs no space up front. Destroying the resource destroys the clone, not the snapshot. The snapshot cannot be destroyed while the clone exists unless it is destroyed deferred.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "truenas_dataset" "golden" {
  name = "tank/golden"
}

resource "truenas_snapshot" "golden_v1" {
  dataset = truenas_dataset.golden.name
  name    = "v1"
}

# A throwaway copy of the golden dataset, created instantly and sharing its
# blocks until written to. Reference the snapshot by id so Terraform creates
# it first and destroys the clone before it.
resource "truenas_snapshot_clone" "test1" {
  snapshot = truenas_snapshot.golden_v1.id
  dataset  = "tank/scratch/test1"

  dataset_properties = {
    compression = "lz4"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `dataset` (String) Name of the dataset or zvol to create, e.g. tank/vms/test1. It must be in the same pool as the snapshot and must not exist yet.
- `snapshot` (String) Full name of the snapshot to clone, e.g. tank/golden@v1.

### Optional

- `dataset_properties` (Map of String) ZFS properties to set on the clone when it is created, as property name to value (e.g. { compression = "lz4" }). Write-only: not read back, so later changes made outside Terraform are not detected. Changing it re-creates the clone.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The clone's dataset name (same as dataset).
- `mountpoint` (String) The clone's mountpoint (empty for a zvol).
- `pool` (String) Name of the pool containing the clone.
- `type` (String) FILESYSTEM or VOLUME, following the cloned snapshot's dataset.
